title: Occupational exposure to cement dust and potential pulmonary and systemic effects.
abstract: Cement production is a major source of occupational exposure to airborne particles, yet detailed characterization of exposure and associated health effects remains limited. Emissions and worker exposures were assessed during clinker mineral production, cement grinding, and bagging using filter-based sampling and direct-reading instruments. title: Nitrous Oxide-Associated Rhabdomyolysis With Acute Kidney Injury Requiring Hemodialysis.
abstract: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is increasingly abused for its euphoric effects, yet its potential for severe medical toxicity remains underrecognized. This case report describes a 22-year-old male who developed severe rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury (AKI) following chronic nitrous oxide abuse. Upon admission, the patient exhibited significant muscle edema and a profoundly elevated creatine kinase level exceeding 45,000 U/L. title: Laparoscopic Bilateral Mesh Removal for Persistent Mesh Infection after Bilateral Transabdominal Preperitoneal Inguinal Hernia Repair: A Case Report.
abstract: Mesh infection after laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair is uncommon and may require mesh removal when drainage and antimicrobial therapy fail. Reports of infection involving both preperitoneal meshes and their midline overlap after bilateral transabdominal preperitoneal repair are scarce. A 70-year-old man developed right suprapubic swelling after bilateral transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repair. title: Serum creatinine- and cystatin C-derived sarcopenia-related indices and the risk of all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as an important predictor of adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, the prognostic relevance of sarcopenia-related indices derived from serum creatinine and cystatin C in patients undergoing TAVI has not been fully established. title: Incidence of and Factors Associated with Hypokalemia During Sulbactam/Ampicillin Therapy: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: The antimicrobial agent sulbactam/ampicillin (SBT/ABPC) is used to treat a wide range of infections; however, hypokalemia has recently attracted attention as an adverse event of SBT/ABPC. Risk factors for this condition have not been fully characterized, and preventive strategies remain unclear. To investigate the incidence of hypokalemia and identify factors associated with its occurrence during sulbactam/ampicillin therapy. title: Neutrophil-hitchhiking and microglia-homing liposomes co-delivering artemisinin and edaravone for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury treatment.
abstract: Clinical outcomes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remain unsatisfactory, largely because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts the delivery of most neuroprotective agents to the brain parenchyma. Although artemisinin (ART) and edaravone (EDV) have shown promising therapeutic potential for CIRI, their clinical application is hindered by their short in vivo half-lives and poor aqueous solubility. title: M2-like-microglia membrane-modified Chuanxiong essential oil liposomes regulate microglial polarization to improve neuroinflammation.
abstract: Ischemic stroke presents a major therapeutic challenge, where modulating microglial polarization is a promising strategy. To enhance the brain delivery and targeting of Chuanxiong essential oil (CXEO), we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform, CXEO-loaded liposomes hybridized with M2-like-microglia membranes (CXEO-LP@M2M). title: Pancreatic surgery in children: nationwide retrospective observational study.
abstract: Paediatric patients differ in various ways from adult populations, but comprehensive multicentre or population-based data are missing for paediatric pancreatic surgery. This study evaluated indications, procedures, complications, and mortality in paediatric patients undergoing pancreatic surgery. title: Pregnancy outcomes following fetal shunt placement in twin gestations.
abstract: Fetal shunt placement in twins remains controversial due to technical difficulties and potential procedure-related risks to the healthy co-twin. We report outcomes following referral for possible shunt placement in twin gestations. This was a retrospective cohort study of twin gestations referred for shunt placement at a single center (2007-2023). title: 2025 Annual Australian Measles and Rubella Genotyping Surveillance Program Report.
abstract: Molecular characterisation is a critical component of Australia's measles and rubella surveillance systems, supporting outbreak investigations, identifying sources of infection, and providing evidence for the continued maintenance of Australia's measles and rubella elimination status.
